messages:
Noah (Finance): Dropping a quick follow-up from today's AH on runway & spend controls. Post questions here and I'll summarize.
Iris (Product): Thanks Noah. Can you share the assumptions behind the new 'conservative' runway number?
Noah (Finance): Conservative assumes flat growth for next 4 quarters, 15% reduction in hiring pace, and no new large enterprise deals. That gives ~11 months of runway vs base case 15 months.
Diego (Eng): Does the conservative plan include toggling Dedicated GPU autoscaling down? Curious what infra ops changes are assumed.
Noah (Finance): Yes. It assumes reducing burst reserve by 40% and aggressive KV cache tuning to save ~12% infra cost.
Leah (Sales): If we accelerate large deals (enterprise closes early), how will that be applied to runway math? Do we net it immediately?
Noah (Finance): We model recognized revenue timing conservatively. If a deal closes early and invoiced, we reflect it immediately in the cash model; pipeline alone doesn't change runway until signed/committed.
Tess (Legal): Any procurement policy changes we should expect from Legal POV? Approval SLAs?
Noah (Finance): Short answer: tighter reviews for non-recurring vendor spend. Legal will be looped in for >$75k new vendors. We'll also require SOC2/DP contracts for any vendor with customer-data access.
Sam (CEO): Focus note: we want nimbleness for revenue-driving experiments. Finance, please carve out a small discretionary bucket managers can access for customer experiments.
Noah (Finance): Agreed. Proposal: a $50k/month discretionary pool split across product & sales experiments; requires 2-sentence justification and manager + finance lead signoff. Thoughts?
Iris (Product): That seems reasonable. Can we allow a 30-day retroactive tag for urgent experiments? Some pilots need faster turn.
Noah (Finance): Fine for <$10k. Retroactive >$10k needs VP signoff.
Diego (Eng): Practical ask: if infra spikes unexpectedly due to a test, what's the emergency approval path?
Noah (Finance): Emergency: manager posts in #spend-approvals, pings finance on-call. Finance grants temporary allowance up to $25k with a 72-hour mitigation plan. >$25k goes to VP review.
Leah (Sales): About vendor onboarding speed 12 We lost a deal last quarter due to a 3-week vendor legal delay. Can we streamline for sales-critical vendors?
Tess (Legal): Agree. We'll add a "fast-track" checklist: pre-approved templates, minimal attachments, and 48-hour SLA for initial review if sales marks vendor as time-sensitive.
Noah (Finance): Operational note: finance-bot will post a weekly "committed spends" snapshot every Monday so teams know upcoming cash obligations.
finance-bot: Posted: 'Committed spend snapshot' https://files.redwood/finance/committed-weekly-2026-03-23.pdf
Iris (Product): One more on capital vs operational: are Dedicated contracts being treated as CapEx? We need clarity for product proposals.
Noah (Finance): We treat multi-month reserved commitments as operating cash outflows (they hit cash immediately if prepaid), but for internal project ROI we amortize over contract term. We'll add a short note to the FAQ.
Sam (CEO): Thanks. Noah, please publish the discretionary pool rules and the emergency spend path by EOD. Also include the fast-track vendor checklist with Legal.
Noah (Finance): Will do. I'll post in #all-hands-followups and pin.
Leah (Sales): Appreciate it. Also can we get a one-pager for managers explaining how to classify "experiment" vs "feature" spend? That would help approvals.
Noah (Finance): Good idea. I'll draft that with Product ops.
Diego (Eng): Thanks. Small ask 12 can we get a sample mitigation plan template for emergency infra overages? Makes approvals faster.
Noah (Finance): I'll attach a template to the spend-approvals channel.
Iris (Product): Thanks all. Short, actionable thread.
Sam (CEO): Nice work. Keep feedback coming.
Noah (Finance): Closing note: if anyone wants a 1:1 walkthrough of their team's spend profile, book time with FP&A via the calendar link in the AH slides.
